decision: platform-code-finding: adopt shared structured CLI error formatting for cli-core scenario CLIs. Proposed change: add a cli-core error presenter that detects cliutil.APIError via errors.As and prints FormatConcise (or equivalent triage fields) before falling back to current error text; update prompt-manager CLI bootstrap to use it; add a CLI-level contract test that a structured HTTP 400 body surfaces code, recovery_hint, and manual_steps in stderr. Target destination: docs/infra-health instrumentation/signal plan and subsequent platform backlog.
rationale: Evidence from 2026-05-13 cli-core audit: cliutil.APIError carries Code, RecoveryHint, AutoFix, and ManualSteps and FormatConcise is tested, but prompt-manager main prints app.Run errors with raw %v. A measured local fixture returning HTTP 400 with code/recovery/manual_steps produced only Last error: api error (400): fixture failure. This loses operator recovery guidance and weakens agent-facing diagnostics for every scenario CLI using cli-core.
notes: Accepted by operator during 2026-05-14 morning vision walk. Adopt shared cli-core error presenter so structured API errors surface code, recovery_hint, and manual_steps instead of raw %v text.

decision: instrumentation-gap: expose active heartbeat run inspection and stop controls in the prompt-manager CLI. Proposed change: add operator-facing CLI commands for GET /heartbeats/running and POST /heartbeats/running/{teamId}/{agentId}/stop, with JSON and human output, conservative stop wording, and CLI contract tests; then update cli/parity/coverage.json to mark both routes covered. Target destination: docs/infra-health instrumentation/signal plan and platform backlog.
rationale: Evidence from the 2026-05-15 cli-scenario-lifecycle audit: the heartbeat API already registers and implements global active-run inspection and stop endpoints, returning RunningAgentsResponse/StopAgentResponse and cancelling/unregistering active runs, but scenarios/prompt-manager/cli/teams/teams.go exposes only heartbeat config/list/enable/disable/trigger/logs and queue-clear. The parity map labels GET /heartbeats/running and POST /heartbeats/running/{teamId}/{agentId}/stop as audit-pending. Measured checks passed, and parity progress still shows 53 audit-pending routes, including these two lifecycle recovery surfaces. Without CLI coverage, operators may reach for queue-clear bookkeeping instead of the safer stop API during incidents.

decision: runtime-health-finding: make autoheal scenario restart actions lock-aware and reconcile health after restart timeouts before retrying. Proposed change: update the autoheal restart policy/backlog target so scenario restart actions detect lifecycle lock failures, record the lock holder, back off instead of immediately counting another restart failure, and run a post-timeout status reconciliation before scheduling another restart for the same scenario. Target destination: docs/infra-health runtime reliability targets / instrumentation roadmap and platform backlog.
rationale: Evidence from measured 2026-05-15 runtime-health heartbeat: latest 50 'vrooli-autoheal actions history --json' records contained 40 failures and 10 successes; 32 failures were 'action timed out' and 7 were 'exit status 1'. The exit-status failures included web-console and agent-manager outputs saying 'Scenario restart blocked by concurrent invocation' with held pids. Over the same 24h, 'vrooli-autoheal actions transitions --json' showed 50 transitions led by web-console with 8 status changes and repeated ok->critical / critical->ok pairs, while several timeout failures were followed by later healthy transitions. This suggests autoheal is treating slow or already-in-flight lifecycle work as fresh failures instead of reconciling status and applying lock-aware backoff.

decision: cross-platform-debt: bring prompt-manager Windows CLI setup to parity with Unix and peer scenario installers. Proposed change: update scenarios/prompt-manager/cli/install.ps1 to pass -ModulePath scenarios/prompt-manager/cli, -Name prompt-manager, and -Manifest scenarios/prompt-manager/.vrooli/service.json to packages/cli-core/install.ps1; extend packages/cli-core/install.ps1 or its contract tests so PowerShell installs honor manifest-declared cli.freshness.inputs and context-root the same way install.sh does; add a repository/static contract test that flags scenario install.ps1 wrappers missing -Manifest when service.json declares cli.freshness. Target destination: docs/infra-health cross-platform portability ledger and platform backlog.
rationale: Evidence from the 2026-05-16 cli-setup audit: prompt-manager's Unix installer passes --manifest scenarios/prompt-manager/.vrooli/service.json, and the service manifest declares cli.freshness.inputs [cli/**, .vrooli/service.json]. The shared Unix installer reads those inputs and forwards --manifest, --context-root, and repeated --freshness-input to cli-installer. The shared PowerShell installer supports -Manifest and forwards --manifest, but prompt-manager's install.ps1 calls it with only the module path and -Name. Peer scenario PowerShell wrappers such as data-backup-manager and many others pass -Manifest. Since NewStandardScenarioApp's runtime stale checker defaults to context .. with inputs cli/** and .vrooli/service.json, a Windows build installed without the manifest/freshness contract can miss the installed runtime manifest and disagree with runtime freshness checks, producing stale warnings or rebuild-loop behavior. Targeted checks: packages/cli-core go test ./cmd/cli-installer and ./cliapp passed; ./cliutil has an existing unrelated env/API-base test failure, so full verification remains pending.

decision: runtime-health-finding: classify scenario CLI discovery and manifest parse failures as permanent configuration defects in autoheal restart handling. Proposed change: update autoheal restart policy/backlog target so errors such as malformed .vrooli/service.json or scenario CLI discovery parse failures are recorded with a permanent_config_failure class, suppress immediate restart retries for that scenario/error tuple, keep the health check status separate from remediation capability, and route a scenario-quality bug/incident payload containing scenario id, manifest path, parse error, action id, and last status transition. Target destination: docs/infra-health runtime reliability targets / instrumentation roadmap and platform backlog.
rationale: Evidence from measured 2026-05-16 runtime-health heartbeat: latest 50 autoheal actions contained 42 failures and 8 successes; scenario-web-console had 8 failures. The two newest web-console restart actions, IDs 11003 at 2026-05-16T22:00:59Z and 11004 at 2026-05-16T22:21:10Z, both failed in 4ms with exit status 1 before lifecycle work began because scenario CLI discovery could not parse /home/matthalloran8/Vrooli/scenarios/web-console/.vrooli/service.json: invalid character ']' looking for beginning of value. Transitions show web-console moved ok->critical at 22:00:36Z and critical->ok at 22:22:36Z; 24h trends show currentStatus ok with 716 ok and 13 critical checks. This means a deterministic scenario artifact defect blocked autoheal's restart remediation path while health later recovered through another path. Treating this as a generic restart failure invites retry noise and hides the permanent config defect from the owning scenario-quality workflow.

decision: platform-code-finding: make lifecycle Stop/Restart cleanup complete bookkeeping even when ports remain bound. Proposed change: refactor internal/lifecycle.cleanupScenarioRuntimeWithRegistry so verifyPortsReleased errors are captured but do not prevent r.Ports.RemoveScenarioLocks or runtimeStop.finish from running; return an aggregated error that preserves the still-bound port diagnostic plus any cleanup failures. Add a lifecycle contract test with a persistent listener/fake runtime store proving Stop returns a still-bound error while legacy port locks are removed and runtime claims/leases are released/stopped. Target destination: docs/infra-health runtime reliability targets / platform backlog.
rationale: Evidence from the 2026-05-17 lifecycle-internals audit: internal/lifecycle/lifecycle.go calls verifyPortsReleased at lines 684-685 and returns immediately on failure; the subsequent cleanup calls at lines 688-691 remove scenario port locks and finish the runtime stop session. verifyPortsReleased documents at lines 837-840 that partial stop should continue to lock cleanup so everything possible is torn down. runtimeStop.finish in internal/lifecycle/runtime_registry.go lines 302-314 releases active port claims and stops runtime leases. Current tests cover verifyPortsReleased directly and normal Stop finalization, but not the still-bound cleanup-order contract. A stuck process during Stop/Restart can therefore leave stale lock files plus active runtime claims/leases, causing retries to see registry/port collisions instead of a clean still-bound-process diagnostic. Focused tests for TestVerifyPortsReleased and TestAcquireScenarioLock passed; full go test ./internal/lifecycle was blocked by this sandbox's read-only runtime-registry SQLite open failure under VROOLI_SANDBOX_MERGED.

decision: instrumentation-gap: make system-mce-recent capability-aware for installed ras-mc-ctl variants and host-access limits. Proposed change: update the MCE telemetry probe/backlog target so it feature-detects /usr/sbin/ras-mc-ctl options before invoking time-window flags, avoids unsupported --since on binaries that do not advertise it, falls back to supported summary/errors/error-count/status modes when safe, and emits structured coverage states such as unsupported_option, rasdaemon_db_inaccessible, edac_unavailable, no_recent_mce, and mce_detected instead of a generic autoheal_failure. Target destination: docs/infra-health instrumentation/signal plan and platform backlog.
rationale: Evidence from measured 2026-05-17 runtime-health heartbeat: durable incident inc_f96059ef8a0652850dc31150 has been open since 2026-05-09T02:04:51Z, last seen 2026-05-17T23:29:32Z, with 380 observations and diagnosis Machine-check telemetry coverage is incomplete. Autoheal status for system-mce-recent is warning while rasdaemonAvailable, rasdaemonServiceActive, and rasdaemonServiceState are all true/active, but the probe output begins Unknown option: since. The installed /usr/sbin/ras-mc-ctl --help lists summary, errors, error-count, status, vendor modes, and help, with no --since option. 24h trends show system-mce-recent total 243, ok 0, warning 243, critical 0, uptimePercent 0, currentStatus warning. Direct fallback probes in this context showed additional host capability/access limits: --summary cannot open /var/lib/rasdaemon/ras-mc_event.db, --status reports drivers not loaded, and --error-count cannot read /dev/mem/sysfs EDAC. The current probe therefore conflates an unsupported CLI flag and host telemetry coverage limits with actual machine-check findings, creating a persistent warning without actionable classification.
